gap: No result ChatGPT got says that HyperX's own store sells the wired Cloud III, which works on Xbox, for $57.99, while the $149.99 Cloud III Wireless next to it is listed only for 'PC, PS5, and Nintendo Switch'. A shopper who upgrades ChatGPT's 'best wired' pick to the wireless version gets a headset HyperX does not list for Xbox.
standout_why: TechRadar (updated 2026-08-28) lists the Arctis Nova Pro Omni, Corsair HS35 v3, Razer BlackShark V3 Pro, Asus ROG Kithara and Arctis Gamebuds. It shows no prices or Xbox connection details in the readable part of the page, and nothing about the Cloud III Wireless. ChatGPT's answer gives only the general warning that ordinary Bluetooth headphones won't carry Xbox game audio. It does not name wireless gaming headsets that leave Xbox out. The two cited pages (RTINGS and Tom's Guide) came back as navigation text only, and Newegg returned 403, so I could not check that those three don't mention the Cloud III Wireless limit. That is why this scores 2 and not 3.
decides: This backs up the cheap end of the page: a wired 3.5 mm headset plugged into the controller ($36.99 EKSA Fenrir S or the $57.99 HyperX Cloud III) is the safe low-cost buy. Among wireless headsets under $150, the Turtle Beach Stealth 600 Gen 3 at $109.99 with an 80 h claim is the priced pick for Xbox. The page should warn that the wireless versions of some headsets that work on Xbox wired (Cloud III Wireless) are not listed for Xbox. Shoppers need the 'X' / Xbox version.
